thread:
Rafael Mendes: Dropping notes here for the lightweight incident review from yesterday (provision-to-ready rollout + metrics/tag explosion). Please add corrections/owners and I’ll turn into Linear comments + action items.

Rafael Mendes: Summary
- What: Provision-to-ready step metrics started emitting high-cardinality labels (per-node identifiers) during early us-east A100 staged rollout.
- Impact: Grafana dashboards slowed/errored; alert evaluation lagged; SRE got noisy signals and some panels were effectively unusable for ~35–45 mins. No customer traffic impact directly, but it reduced our ability to triage nodes stuck in Validating.
- Severity: minor (internal reliability/observability degradation).

Rafael Mendes: Timeline (approx, all times UTC)
- T0 (thread start yesterday): rollout flag enabled for us-east/A100, provision-to-ready pipeline running against new nodes.
- +10m: Sergio/Aisha noticed dashboard queries timing out; alert eval duration spiked.
- +15m: Allison flagged suspected cardinality regression in provisioning step metrics; asked to check recent tag set.
- +20m: Ethan/Benji confirmed readiness service emitting step spans/metrics with node_id-like label.
- +25m: Mitigation: disabled the offending label via config/flag (and paused alerting rules that were paging).
- +35m: Dashboards recovered; alert eval back to normal.
- Later: follow-up PR drafted to remove per-node labels + backfill dashboards.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1 to that. Also worth noting: ops console was still showing counts by state but the per-step breakdown was basically dead during the window. We were flying blind on why nodes were failing Validating.

Aisha Bello: Adding detail from my side:
- The main pain was query timeouts on the “step breakdown” panels + alert rule queries in the same metric family.
- I flipped the paging rule to ticket-only while we mitigated (per Sean’s earlier guidance). We should document that as the recommended first move during rollout.

Allison Grant: Root cause hypothesis (confirmed via label inspection): we had `node`/`instance_id`/`hostname` (or equivalent) included as a label on step timing + failure metrics. That blew up series count fast with churn from provisioning.

Allison Grant: Contributing factor: we reviewed metric names, but not a hard checklist for label cardinality. Also we didn’t have a canary/gate that rejects metrics with per-node identifiers.

Sergio Costa: I pulled one of the scraped series examples from Prom:
`redwood_provision_step_duration_seconds{step="validate_nccl",region="us-east",pool="dedicated",node_id="ip-10-12-34-56",image="candidate"} 12.3`
That `node_id` label was the killer.

Ethan Park: Confirming from control-plane side: this came in with the initial metrics/tracing PR. We intended the node_id only in logs/traces, not as a metric label. We’ll change to keep node info in trace attributes (sampled) and emit metrics aggregated by {step,region,gpu_type,image_channel}.

Benji Okafor: For the incident review: we also saw readiness artifacts storage grow faster because failures were spamming with unique keys. Not catastrophic, but it’s tied to the same “unique per node” data flow.

Miles Thornton: SLO angle: this didn’t violate the time-to-ready SLO directly, but it *did* make the SLI harder to trust/operate in the moment. We should call out “observability dependency” as part of the rollout readiness checklist.

Rafael Mendes: Proposed contributing factors (please edit)
- Missing cardinality checklist during metric review; labels weren’t stress-tested under churn.
- Rollout happens exactly when churn is highest (lots of nodes), so issues amplify.
- Alerting rules were enabled early; no initial “observe-only” period for the new metric family.

Vanessa Ortiz: Another contrib factor: the dashboards used `sum by (node_id)` panels for debugging during dev, and that accidentally got promoted to the shared dashboard pack. We should keep per-node debugging in logs/traces, not shared dashboards.

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup: also I’d like an explicit “safe labels” table in the dashboard PR review (region/gpu_type/pool/step/image_channel yes; node_id/hostname no).

Rafael Mendes: Action items draft (owners + where to track)
1) Remove per-node labels from provisioning metrics; keep node identifiers only in logs/traces (Owner: Ethan/Benji) [PR already in flight]
2) Update Grafana dashboards to stop referencing per-node labels + adjust panels to use aggregated dimensions (Owner: Sergio)
3) Add a metric review checklist + lint/guardrail for common cardinality foot-guns (Owner: Allison)
4) Update rollout runbook: during staged rollout, new alerts start ticket-only for 48h; paging enabled after baseline verified (Owner: Aisha)
5) Add “observability readiness” gate to rollout checklist (dashboards load, alert eval < Xs, series count within bounds) (Owner: Miles/Rafael)
6) Backlog: tune validation flakes/timeouts separately (ENG-4830) so we don’t conflate real failures with observability issues (Owner: Vanessa)

Sergio Costa: For (2) I’ll add a note: we should backfill the step breakdown dashboard with the new label set so it doesn’t look “empty” after the fix. I can handle.

Allison Grant: For (3) I can write the checklist + add to the observability PR template. Not sure we can lint all metrics in CI quickly, but we can at least block obvious `node_id`/`pod` labels in review.

Incident Bot: Reminder: if you want this linked as a post-incident note, include: Impact, Root Cause, Detection, Mitigation, Prevention.

Rafael Mendes: Good call. I’ll format the final note with those headings.

Rafael Mendes: Detection
- Detected via Grafana query timeouts + alert eval duration spikes (not via a dedicated “series explosion” alert).

Rafael Mendes: Mitigation
- Disabled offending label/config; temporarily reduced alert severity to avoid paging noise during mitigation.

Rafael Mendes: Prevention
- Merge PR removing per-node metric labels.
- Add checklist + alert/dash rollout policy.

Vanessa Ortiz: Please add that the staged rollout kill switch worked as intended (feature flag to disable metrics emission +/orchestrator step tags). That was a win.

Ethan Park: +1. We should keep that as an explicit design requirement going forward: any new telemetry path must have a kill switch.

Aisha Bello: Also suggest a small alert for “unique series count” on the new metric namespace. Even a coarse one would have caught this earlier.

Allison Grant: I’ll look at what we can do without a bunch of false positives. Maybe alert on sudden slope change rather than absolute series count.

Rafael Mendes: Next steps
- I’ll post the cleaned summary back here later today + link the Linear items once created/updated. If anyone has logs/screenshots that help (e.g., Grafana error, Prom series count), drop them in this thread.

Sergio Costa: I’ll attach screenshots in Linear (don’t want to spam here), but TL;DR was “504 gateway timeout” and panel load > 30s.

Miles Thornton: Make sure the review note explicitly says “no customer-facing outage,” but operational risk during rollout was real. That nuance matters.

Rafael Mendes: Will do. Thanks all.
